scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: prismis analyzes everything its sources publish (docs/IDEA.md); this turns a page that is refused every cycle into a stored, summarized item, and records when the summary covers part of it.
scrutiny.failureCase: An oversized page still never stored.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: the kind classifier already bounds its request (kind_classifier.py:59-63); llm_call.py is the shared LLM-call module summarizer and evaluator import; build_llm_analysis (analysis.py:78) is the one analysis assembler. The design extends each rather than adding a parallel path.
scrutiny.failureCase: A second bounding scheme beside the kind classifier's, or a record written outside build_llm_analysis.

scrutiny.test: T2 same noun: the byte-over-token guarantee is about byte-level BPE, the tokenizer family OpenAI models (gpt-5.4-nano via OpenRouter) use; the measurement that motivated it is the provider's own refusal count for this exact page (482,792 tokens for 1,724,631 bytes).
scrutiny.failureCase: A character ratio from English prose stood in for the pathological page.

scrutiny.test: T3 degrade: 8 of 39,022 stored items would be summarized from their first 350,000 bytes on re-analysis, recorded; stated as a sacrifice.
scrutiny.failureCase: A cut that is silent or unrecorded.

scrutiny.test: T5 running system: the post-deploy commitment reads cerebro's next cycle for an article over the bound stored with content_bounded; the defect walk reproduces the refusal with a stub that enforces the window in bytes.
scrutiny.failureCase: Only a fixture built to pass.

scrutiny.test: T6 assumptions: 50,000 tokens of headroom covers the system prompts, context.md (3,001 bytes on cerebro) and the reply; the tokenizer is byte-level BPE.

T7 consumers, enumerated with grep for summarize_with_analysis, evaluate_content and .extract(: the orchestrator (orchestrator.py 142, 160, 239), the CLI's analyze repair (cli/src/cli/analyze.py 176, 191) and the API's on-demand extract; bounding inside the components covers all of them. content_bounded is a new additive key with no reader yet.
scrutiny.failureCase: A caller that bypasses the bound.

scrutiny.test: T9 six months: MAX_CONTENT_BYTES is tied to the deployed model's window; a smaller-window model needs it lowered, accepted in the sacrifices, and its overflow fails at the existing per-item boundary rather than silently.
T10 reversibility: a revert; no schema change, an additive analysis key.

T11 class, every LLM call site enumerated with grep for call_llm_with_circuit_breaker(, complete( and .classify(: summarizer, evaluator, deep extractor send article text (bounded here); kind classifier already caps; context_analyzer, context_auto_updater and audio send summaries or per-item snippets ([:200], top-5 lists), not article text. Python is the only stack that calls an LLM; engines axis n/a.
scrutiny.failureCase: Another call site sending unbounded article text.

scrutiny.test: T12 new state: content_bounded distinguishes a summary of part of a page from one of the whole, which Principle II requires; nothing else records it.
T13 two places: one helper computes the bound; the summarizer's word count reads full content for mode selection, a different fact.
scrutiny.failureCase: The bound computed separately per call site.

scrutiny.test: T18 cause: the cause is the prompt carrying unbounded text; bounding it removes the refusal for every page, rather than special-casing ascii.rest or catching the 400.
scrutiny.failureCase: Matching the provider's context-length message and retrying.

scrutiny.test: T20 walk: ascii.rest, 1,724,631 bytes, is cut at 350,000 bytes on a character boundary (about 98,000 tokens at its measured 3.57 bytes per token), the prompt notes the cut, the summary returns, the summarizer metadata carries content_bounded {350000-ish, 1724631}, build_llm_analysis copies it, and the item stores with its full content; the next cycle finds it stored and skips it.
scrutiny.failureCase: A step that drops the record or the full content.
